findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "create_quote_link" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Create a Quote Link: a web page where the user's customer sees a quote for a job, picks one of up to 4 options and any add-ons, types their name, and approves, …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_quote_link" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Create a Quote Link: a web page where the user's customer sees a quote for a job, picks one of up to 4 options and any add-ons, types their name, and approves, …

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_quote_link, get_quote_status · Private data: create_quote_link, get_quote_status, cancel_quote_link · Public sink: create_quote_link, revise_quote_link.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_quote_link, get_quote_status · Private data: create_quote_link, get_quote_status, cancel_quote_link · Public sink: create_quote_link, revise_quote_link

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
